limitations: An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.
title: At the Highest Point, is Acceleration Zero?
story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it climbs, pauses for a brief fraction of a second at its highest point, and then speeds up on its way back down. Watching it hang motionless at the very top, it is tempting to think that everything stops—that both its velocity and its acceleration must be zero at that exact instant.

Galileo puzzled over these motions and realized that velocity and acceleration do not always do the same thing. Velocity tells you how fast and in what direction the position is changing. At the peak, the ball stops moving upward before it moves downward, so its velocity is momentarily zero. But acceleration tells you how fast the velocity is changing.

Gravity pulls steadily on the ball throughout the entire flight, whether it is moving up, pausing at the top, or falling down. Because gravity does not turn off at the peak, the velocity is continually decreasing at a constant rate. At the top, the velocity is zero, but its rate of change—the acceleration—is still directed downward at $9.8\text{ m/s}^2$.
cardDescription: Explore a vertical throw where velocity drops to zero at the peak, but gravity keeps a constant downward acceleration of $g$.
instructions: Press play to watch the throw. Adjust launch speed and gravity to see how acceleration remains constant.
learningGoal: Explain that the force of gravity is m g and the acceleration is -g at every instant, including the top, so a larger mass changes the force and not the motion.

scene.description: Two equal-width scenes side by side in one frame. Left, the motion: a ball (frame object id ball.toss) on a height ruler fixed to the highest top, zero at the launch mark, up positive, with a blue velocity arrow (vec.v), a separate dashed warm acceleration arrow (vec.a) and a callout (callout.toss) beside it reading velocity, acceleration and the downward gravitational force, plus a state line. Right, velocity over time (plot.vt): the line on fixed scales, a linked marker and a note with the slope. Ball, marker and readings move together. No snapshot strip.

quantities.label: Launch speed
quantities.meaning: Upward speed at the instant of the throw.
quantities.reference: Measured at the launch mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Magnitude of the constant downward acceleration.

quantities.label: Time of the top
quantities.meaning: Elapsed time from launch at which the velocity is zero.

quantities.label: Height of the top
quantities.meaning: Height of the ball at its top above the ground mark.
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Height of the ball
quantities.meaning: Height above the ground mark, up positive; the launch height is its value at t = 0.
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Vertical velocity
quantities.meaning: Signed rate of change of height, up positive; zero at the top.

quantities.label: Vertical acceleration
quantities.meaning: Signed rate of change of velocity: constant and negative (down), -gravity.

quantities.label: Gravitational force
quantities.meaning: Magnitude of the downward force of gravity on the ball (positive, the arrow draws it down).

observations.text: The velocity follows the straight line v = u - g t and is zero at the top.
The slope of the velocity line is -gravity at every instant, so the acceleration is nonzero at the top.
The force at the top is mass times gravity, while the trajectory and the velocity graph stay identical.
A faster toss or a weaker gravity moves the top later and higher on the fixed scales.

checkpoints.label: 0.10 s before the top
checkpoints.expected: Velocity positive, acceleration -gravity, force mass times gravity.

checkpoints.label: At the top
checkpoints.expected: The velocity is zero, the acceleration -gravity and the force mass times gravity, downward.

checkpoints.label: At the top with the largest mass
checkpoints.expected: The force is larger; velocity, acceleration and height are exactly as at the default mass.

checkpoints.label: Fast toss, weak gravity, at the top
checkpoints.expected: At the fastest toss and the weakest gravity the top comes later and higher; velocity zero, acceleration -gravity.

mode.initialState: Launch speed 5 m/s, gravity 9.8 m/s^2, mass 1 kg; the ball at the launch mark, time 0.000 s, paused.

controls.label: Play
controls.purpose: Run the motion and replay it.
controls.selectionReason: Time explains the change, and the one supported transport drives every linked view.

controls.label: Time since launch
controls.purpose: Inspect any instant of the motion.
controls.selectionReason: A scrubber lets the learner stop on the instants the explanation compares.

controls.label: Launch speed
controls.purpose: See how the speed of the toss moves the top without changing what gravity does there.
controls.selectionReason: The speed varies continuously and intermediate speeds show that the top moves while the pull does not; two named cases would hide that.

controls.label: Gravity
controls.purpose: See that a different gravity changes the acceleration and the time to the top, not the idea.
controls.selectionReason: Gravity varies continuously and the learner can compare nearby values; two planets would hide that.

controls.label: Mass
controls.purpose: See that mass changes the force of gravity and leaves the acceleration and the motion unchanged.
controls.selectionReason: The mass varies continuously, and the learner changes it while paused at the top to compare force and acceleration at the same instant.

controls.label: At top
controls.purpose: Jump to the top of the toss and pause there.
controls.selectionReason: The top is the one instant the explanation is about; a button reaches it exactly, which dragging the scrubber does not.
controls.effect: Seeks the top marker and pauses.

controls.label: Reset experiment
controls.selectionReason: Replay keeps the settings; Reset restores them so the learner can start over.
controls.effect: Restores launch speed 5 m/s, gravity 9.8 m/s^2, mass 1 kg and time 0, paused.

claims.text: The gravitational force is m g and the acceleration is -g at every instant, so doubling the mass doubles the force and leaves the motion unchanged.
claims.check: a = F / m = -m g / m = -g; v = u - g t and y = u t - g t^2 / 2 do not contain m.

assumptions: No air resistance, up is positive.
